answer: Save the lowest offset not yet written, the low-water mark just below the first unfinished record, not the highest finished offset. Commit only after the writer accepts a record. A crash then replays everything from that point, so duplicated work is possible but nothing is lost. If you save the highest finished position instead, any record below it that is still in flight when the crash hits is skipped on restart, because its offset was already committed. Those records are lost silently (at-most-once behavior). Source: pa_pattern_backpressure_scaling.md, around L161.
